chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-02.proposition: Secular Western Europe compares favorably with the more religious United States on several social harms, undermining the claim that greater religiosity reliably produces stronger family values.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-03.proposition: Comprehensive factual education about world religions would prevent enforced ignorance and test religious traditions through free information, disrupting toxic forms while permitting benign forms to survive.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-04.proposition: Religions are human inventions resembling languages and music: collectively produced cultural traditions that continually arise, change, evolve, and disappear.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-06.proposition: The concept of God has evolved from a concrete anthropomorphic ruler into an increasingly abstract and featureless entity, evidencing continuing human conceptual revision.

chunk-002:chunk002-candidate-04.proposition: A beginning of space and time in the Big Bang does not establish divine creation, and positing God introduces an even greater unexplained being.

chunk-002:chunk002-candidate-05.proposition: Observers necessarily find themselves in a life-permitting universe, so anthropic selection and the possibility of other universes remove the need to infer an intelligent fine-tuner.

chunk-002:chunk002-candidate-06.proposition: The alleged impossibility of Darwinian explanations for free will, consciousness, choice, and intentionality is merely asserted despite substantial work developing such explanations.

chunk-002:chunk002-candidate-09.proposition: Testable naturalistic explanations of fine-tuning remain possible, whereas an intelligent creator is unnecessary and demands a more extravagant explanation of its own existence.

chunk-002:chunk002-candidate-10.proposition: Morality can arise through human reasoning and cultural development without God, whose alleged commands reach people only through fallible human representatives.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-03.proposition: Invoking creation outside nature is unintelligible because the concept of creating derives its meaning from causal regularities within the natural world.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-07.proposition: Consciousness is scientifically investigable and reducible through shared evidence, theory, and mechanistic explanation rather than an irreducible subjective foundation for analogous belief in God.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-06.proposition: Scientific and academic inquiry confront the possibility of error, whereas religious communities often discourage believers from questioning faith, giving corrigible inquiry the epistemic advantage.
